'''Rolando Basim Chuaqui Kettlun''' (December 30, 1935–April 23, 1994<ref name="pro">{{cite journal |title=Rolando Chuaqui Kettlun |journal=Proyecciones (Antofagasta) |date=1994 |volume=13 |issue=1 |doi=10.22199/S07160917.1994.0001.00001 |url=https://www.revistaproyecciones.cl/article/view/2637 |access-date=3 March 2022|doi-access=free }}</ref>) was a [[Chilean people|Chilean]] [[mathematician]] who worked on the foundations of probabilities and foundations of mathematics. Throughout his lifetime, he published two books and over 50 journal articles in mathematics and logic.<ref name="pro"/> He also spearheaded the creation and expansion of mathematics departments across multiple Chilean universities.

==Biography==
Chuaqui was born into a [[Syrians|Syrian]] immigrant family from [[Homs]] in [[Syria]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wilfredo Quezada Y Carlo Apablaza - Autores |url=https://ediciones.uc.cl/autores/wilfredo-quezada-y-carlo-apablaza.html |access-date=2023-12-25 |website=ediciones.uc.cl}}</ref> He entered the [[University of Chile]] in 1953 to study medicine. He obtained a Ph.D. in Logic and the Methodology of Science, an interdisciplinary program between the Department of Mathematics and Department of Philosophy, from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1965. His doctoral advisor was [[David Blackwell]]. Chuaqui returned to Chile after graduating, serving as a professor at the University of Chile and then the [[Pontifical Catholic University of Chile]]. During his time at the Pontifical Catholic, he advised three doctoral students.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rolando Chuaqui - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=22578 |website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu |access-date=3 March 2022}}</ref>

Chuaqui held several visiting positions, including at UCLA (1967), [[Princeton University]] (1970), [[University of São Paulo]] (1971 and 1982), [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1973–74), [[University of Campinas]] (1976, 1977 and 1978), [[Stanford University]] (1984), and [[San Jose State University|San José State University]] (1986-89).

He was a long-term collaborator of [[Patrick Suppes]], with whom he worked on non-standard analysis and measurement in sciences.<ref>[http://www.jornadaschuaqui.mat.uc.cl/vida/ Life and Work of Rolando Chuaqui Kettlun] (in Spanish), Jornados Rolando Chuaqui Kettlun, retrieved 2017-03-25.</ref> In 1986, he proposed a mathematical formulation for [[Pragmatic theory of truth|pragmatic truth]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mikenberg |first1=Irene |last2=da Costa |first2=Newton C. A. |last3=Chuaqui |first3=Rolando |title=Pragmatic truth and approximation to truth |journal=Journal of Symbolic Logic |date=March 1986 |volume=51 |issue=1 |pages=201–221 |doi=10.2307/2273956}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
He was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in Mathematics in 1983.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rolando Chuaqui Kettlun |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/rolando-chuaqui-kettlun/ |website=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation |access-date=2 March 2022}}</ref>

Since 1999, a series of annual research conferences in Chile, known as the ''Jornadas Rolando Chuaqui Kettlun'', is held in his memory.<ref>[http://www.jornadaschuaqui.mat.uc.cl/ Jornadas Rolando Chuaqui Kettlun: filosofía y ciencias], retrieved 2017-03-25.</ref><ref>{{Cite SEP|url-id=phil-science-latin-america|title=Philosophy of Science in Latin America|last=Cordero|first=Alberto|edition=Winter 2016|editor=[[Eward N. Zalta]]}}</ref> The [[Pontifical Catholic University of Chile]] also has a building named after him, which houses its Department of Mathematics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Facultad de Matemáticas:: Edificio Rolando Chuaqui |url=http://www.mat.uc.cl/edificio-rolando-chuaqui.html |website=www.mat.uc.cl |access-date=2 March 2022}}</ref>
